Subject: Deployment enclosure brief + SIG/CAIQ evidence for procurement review

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As promised, attached is a compact "deployment enclosure" packet that describes how Redwood isolates customer workloads across our Dedicated (reserved capacity) and Private (VPC / on-prem) deployment modes. This is a focused handoff for your security and procurement teams — not the full SOC 2 binder, but the pieces you asked to see first.

Attachments included (short):
- redwood-deployment-enclosure-arch-v1.pdf — narrative and annotated diagrams (control plane vs data plane, connectivity patterns)
- network-diagram-enclosure-v3.png — high-level topology with traffic flows and egress controls
- sig-caiq-mapping-redline.xlsx — mapping of questions we expect to be in scope and our preliminary answers

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- "Enclosure" model: workloads run inside tenant-specific compute planes; control plane is logically separated and restricted by mutual TLS + RBAC and runs on our management plane.
- Data plane isolation: Dedicated customers get reserved GPU pools and per-tenant VPC peering (or VLANs where required); Private customers can run the same runtime inside their VPC or on-prem package.
- Key boundaries: KMS-managed keys reside in customer KMS for Private deployments or in a per-customer envelope key in our KMS for Dedicated (we provide HSM-backed keys upon request). Audit logs (write-once) are retained per contract; retention and export options are configurable.
- SIG/CAIQ approach: we map the most relevant controls (network segmentation, key management, logging, patching) in the attached spreadsheet; items marked "defer" are areas we typically resolve during onboarding (e.g., delivery of tenant-specific network ACLs).

Asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm the scope your security team wants covered in the first pass (SIG Lite vs full CAIQ)?
2) If procurement will need a DocuSign or GSA-style evidence bundle, loop procurement@oakridge-corp.com and we'll push a packaged ZIP (redacted where appropriate).
3) Proposed walkthrough: I can do a 30-min diagram review week of Aug 10 — does Aug 11 10am PT work for your team?

I'll hand the technical follow-ups to Karthik (cc'd) — he's copied in case you want deeper answers on KMS, audit logs, and the kernel-level isolation choices.

Thanks,
Grace

Looping in quick technical clarifications before the walkthrough. Forwarding Samantha's KMS/logging questions inline for visibility.

> "KMS boundary: when you say 'per-customer envelope key in our KMS' for Dedicated, can you confirm whether customers can bring their own key (BYOK) into your platform or if the envelope key is generated by Redwood?"

Answer: For Dedicated customers we support two modes:
- BYOK (recommended for enterprise Dedicated): customer-provisioned CMKs in their cloud KMS; we run the inference runtime in a dedicated subnet and the encryption keys remain in customer KMS. We use an asymmetric wrapping flow so raw model blobs never transit unencrypted.
- Redwood-managed envelope keys: for customers who prefer simpler onboarding, we create a per-tenant envelope key in our HSM-backed KMS. HSM-backed keys and import options are available under enterprise terms.

> "Audit logs: does the write-once export include syscall-level logs or is it limited to application/runtime events and admin ops?"

Answer: Our standard export includes: admin audit trails (API calls, role changes, deployments), runtime request/response metadata (headers, request IDs, token usage), and platform health events. We do not ship raw syscall traces by default. For customers requiring deeper telemetry we can enable agent-level syscall/syslog exports in Private/on-prem installs and map those to the customer's SIEM (shipper config is part of onboarding).

SIG/CAIQ plan:
- We'll produce a full CAIQ crosswalk (requested by Samantha) with attachments for evidence items (diagrams, KMS screenshots, policy excerpts).
- Marissa: can you take point on generating the formal evidence ZIP and mark items that need redaction? I'll annotate the mapping workbook inline to indicate which artifacts we can deliver immediately vs which require a signed NDAs or on-site validation.

Samantha: for the Aug 11 diagram walkthrough we'll bring a short deck that traces a single request end-to-end (hosted -> dedicated/private variations) and show where controls enforce separation.

Thanks,
Karthik
